definitionEn: to dislike someone or something intensely
situation: You feel a very strong dislike for a person, activity or thing, much stronger than ordinary annoyance.

examples.text: I [[detest]] cold showers, but my doctor says they're good for me.
Most of the staff [[detested]] the new manager, who shouted at people in front of clients.
He [[detests]] small talk and usually leaves parties early.

texts: I [[detest]] people who talk during films.
Many teenagers [[detest]] being told what to wear.
Most cats [[detest]] getting wet, but some love it.

badCollocation.noteRu: После detest нужен герундий: I detest waiting. Инфинитив (detest to wait) — ошибка.

collocationTask.explanationRu: С absolutely сочетаются сильные глаголы: absolutely detest, hate, love. Dislike для него слишком слабый, oppose — «выступать против», а mind бывает в вопросах и отрицаниях.

nuance.text: I [[detest]] cruelty of any kind — it makes me feel physically sick.
nuance.explanationRu: Detest — ненавидеть, испытывать отвращение. Dislike — просто «не нравиться», это слишком слабо для того, от чего «физически тошнит».

reverse.text: I slightly [[dislike]] the colour, but the jacket fits perfectly.
reverse.explanationRu: Лёгкая неприязнь — slightly dislike. «Slightly detest» — противоречие: detest всегда означает сильную неприязнь.

fixIt.text: I [[disgust]] people who are cruel to animals.
fixIt.explanationRu: Disgust — «вызывать отвращение»: Cruelty disgusts me. Самому ненавидеть кого-то — detest.

wordFormation.text: Most readers found the novel's villain truly [[detestable]].

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Do you want to join the karaoke night after work on Friday?"
options: Yes! I detest karaoke, it's my favourite thing in the world.
Thanks, but I detest singing in public. I'll come for the food, though!
I must decline, as I find such vocal activities utterly detestable.
reply.explanationRu: Detest singing — терпеть не могу петь, это вежливый отказ. «Detest karaoke, it's my favourite» — противоречие, а третий ответ звучит слишком чопорно для коллеги.

rewrite.original: I really hate getting up early.
rewrite.explanationRu: После detest нужен герундий: detest getting up.

definitionEn: having a harmful or damaging effect on something
situation: You say formally that something harms health, the environment, results or someone's career.

examples.text: Too much screen time can be [[detrimental]] to children's sleep.
The long strike had a [[detrimental]] effect on tourism, and several hotels closed.
Scientists warn that the new dam will prove [[detrimental]] to fish in the river.

texts: Stress is [[detrimental]] to both body and mind.
The decision proved [[detrimental]] to the company's reputation.
Even small amounts of lead are [[detrimental]] to health.

badCollocation.noteRu: Detrimental требует предлога to: detrimental to health. «For» — калька с «вредно для».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Detrimental (или harmful) to your health — вредно для здоровья. Unhealthy не сочетается с to, painful — «болезненный», sickly — «хилый, болезненный на вид».

nuance.text: Long working hours are [[detrimental]] to family life.
nuance.explanationRu: Detrimental — наносящий вред (здоровью, карьере, природе). Hurtful — обидный, ранящий чувства: hurtful remarks.

reverse.text: It was a [[hurtful]] thing to say to someone who had just lost her job.
reverse.explanationRu: Обидные слова — hurtful. Detrimental — про вред делу или здоровью, а не про обиду.

fixIt.text: Air pollution has a [[deteriorating]] effect on children's lungs.
fixIt.explanationRu: Deteriorating — «ухудшающийся» (сам по себе). Вредное воздействие на что-то — a detrimental effect.

wordFormation.text: Working too many hours can be [[detrimental]] to your mental health.

rewrite.explanationRu: Detrimental to something — вредный для чего-то.

definitionEn: to damage or destroy a place, area or economy very badly
senseNote: Эмоциональное be devastated (быть убитым горем) тоже очень частотно; здесь — о разрушении городов, природы, экономики.
situation: A storm, war, fire or economic crisis causes enormous damage to a place, industry or community.

examples.text: The hurricane [[devastated]] the island, destroying almost every home on the coast.
The closure of the steelworks [[devastated]] the town's economy.
A single night of frost can [[devastate]] a vineyard's entire harvest.

texts: Floods [[devastated]] large parts of the region last spring.
The war [[devastated]] the country's roads and railways.
A fire [[devastated]] the historic library in 1986.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Опустошить холодильник» — empty или raid the fridge. Devastate — разрушить, разорить (город, урожай, экономику).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Землетрясение или ураган devastate (или destroy) город. Spoil — испортить, break — сломать предмет, а harm — навредить человеку или здоровью.

nuance.text: The earthquake [[devastated]] the city, and barely a building was left standing.
nuance.explanationRu: Damage — повредить, часто частично. Devastate — разрушить почти полностью, так что «почти ни одного здания не осталось».

reverse.text: The storm slightly [[damaged]] our garden fence.
reverse.explanationRu: Небольшое повреждение — slightly damaged. «Slightly devastated» — противоречие: devastate означает огромные разрушения.

fixIt.text: The wildfire [[demolished]] thousands of hectares of forest in just two days.
fixIt.explanationRu: Demolish — сносить здания, обычно намеренно. Лес, урожай или целые районы разоряет стихия — devastate.

wordFormation.text: Aerial photos showed the full scale of the [[devastation]] after the flood.

rewrite.original: The floods caused terrible damage to the farms in the valley.
rewrite.frame: The farms in the valley ____ by the floods.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the farms were devastated by the floods.

definitionEn: a person, used informally with adjectives like lucky, poor or cheeky
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — дьявол, чёрт. Здесь — разговорное «о человеке»: lucky devil (везунчик), poor devil (бедняга), cheeky devil (нахал).
situation: You talk casually about someone you envy, pity or find cheeky, usually adding a word like lucky or poor.

examples.text: You won a trip to Japan? You lucky [[devil]]!
The poor [[devil]] had to repeat his whole presentation because the recording failed.
Our dog is a cheeky little [[devil]] — he steals socks from the washing basket.

texts: She's off to Bali for a month, the lucky [[devil]].
I felt sorry for the poor [[devil]] who had to clean up after the party.
Come here, you little [[devil]], and give me back my phone!

badCollocation.noteRu: Восклицание «Чёрт!» по-английски — Damn! или Oh no! Devil как ругательство не используют.

collocationTask.prompt: She won the lottery, the lucky ___!
collocationTask.explanationRu: О везунчике говорят the lucky devil (или lucky thing). Demon, hell и ghost в таких выражениях не используются.

nuance.text: The poor [[devil]] had no idea his flight had been cancelled.
nuance.explanationRu: В разговорных фразах о людях (poor devil, lucky devil) используется только devil. Demon — демон, злой дух; «poor demon» звучит как фраза из фэнтези.

fixIt.text: Speak of the [[wolf]] — here comes Anna now!
fixIt.explanationRu: Когда появляется тот, о ком только что говорили, по-английски говорят Speak of the devil (≈ «лёгок на помине»). Волк в этой идиоме не используется.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "Guess what? My boss just gave me a week off AND a bonus!"
options: You poor devil, that sounds absolutely awful.
Please accept my formal congratulations, you fortunate devil.
You lucky devil! Got any plans for the week yet?
reply.explanationRu: Lucky devil — «везунчик», с доброй завистью. Poor devil — «бедняга», для хорошей новости не годится, а formal congratulations рядом с разговорным devil звучит нелепо.

definitionEn: to invent or plan a new method, system or way of doing something
situation: Someone carefully thinks up a new plan, strategy, method or system to solve a problem.

examples.text: The team [[devised]] a clever system for sharing desks, and it saved the company a fortune.
Researchers have [[devised]] a new test that can detect the disease in minutes.
My flatmates and I finally [[devised]] a cleaning rota that everyone sticks to.

texts: Engineers must [[devise]] a safer way to store the waste.
Can you [[devise]] a quiz for the office party?
It took months to [[devise]] a fair system for bonuses.

badCollocation.noteRu: Устройство — device (существительное, с буквой c). Devise (с буквой s) — глагол «разрабатывать».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Devise сочетается с method, plan, scheme, system. Решение, обещание и усилие «делают»: make a decision, make a promise, make an effort.

nuance.text: For the product launch, the marketing team [[devised]] a completely new strategy.
nuance.explanationRu: Devise — придумать и разработать с нуля. Revise — пересмотреть, исправить то, что уже есть; «revise a completely new strategy» — противоречие.

reverse.text: After the complaints, the company [[revised]] its refund policy.
reverse.explanationRu: Существующие правила после жалоб пересматривают: revise. Devise — создать что-то новое, а не исправить старое.

fixIt.text: Scientists have [[invented]] a plan to protect the coral reef from warming seas.
fixIt.explanationRu: Invent — изобрести устройство или выдумать отговорку. План, схему или стратегию разрабатывают: devise a plan.

reply.context: Your manager says: "Customers keep complaining that they wait too long on the phone."
options: Maybe we could devise a call-back system so nobody has to stay on hold.
Let's devise the customers to call back later in the evening.
Yeah, whatever, somebody should devise something, I guess.
reply.explanationRu: Devise a system — разработать систему, это решение проблемы. Devise не значит «советовать» (это advise), а третий ответ звучит небрежно и безразлично для разговора с руководителем.

definitionEn: to identify what illness someone has or what is causing a problem
situation: A doctor, mechanic or other expert examines someone or something and finds out exactly what is wrong.

examples.text: She was [[diagnosed]] with diabetes at the age of twelve.
The mechanic quickly [[diagnosed]] the problem as a faulty battery.
Our IT support team can usually [[diagnose]] network issues remotely.

texts: He was [[diagnosed]] with asthma as a child.
The fault was finally [[diagnosed]] after three visits to the garage.
Her condition was [[diagnosed]] too late for surgery.

badCollocation.noteRu: После diagnose нужен предлог with: diagnose someone with cancer, be diagnosed with cancer.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Diagnose someone with an illness — поставить диагноз. Determine — устанавливать факт, state — заявлять, define — давать определение; с a patient with они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: It took doctors three years to [[diagnose]] her rare condition.
nuance.explanationRu: Examine — осматривать пациента. Diagnose — по результатам осмотра и анализов понять, что это за болезнь.

reverse.text: The nurse will [[examine]] your ankle before the doctor sees you.
reverse.explanationRu: Осмотреть лодыжку — examine. Диагностируют болезнь или неисправность, а не часть тела.

fixIt.text: It took three specialists to [[define]] what was wrong with his heart.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «определить» здесь не define (давать определение), а diagnose — установить, что за болезнь.

wordFormation.text: The hospital has bought new [[diagnostic]] equipment for heart patients.

reply.context: A friend says: "My laptop keeps switching itself off, and I've no idea why."
options: Have you tried diagnosing it with a new charger yet?
It would be prudent to have a qualified technician diagnose the aforementioned malfunction.
Take it to the repair shop. They can usually diagnose the problem in ten minutes.
reply.explanationRu: Diagnose the problem — найти причину неисправности. «Diagnose it with a charger» — бессмыслица, а второй ответ слишком официален для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: the identification of an illness or problem after examining someone or something
situation: A doctor tells a patient exactly what illness they have after tests and an examination.

examples.text: The doctor wants to run more tests before making a [[diagnosis]].
Her cancer [[diagnosis]] came as a shock to the whole family.
The engineer's [[diagnosis]] was simple: the software needed updating.

texts: A wrong [[diagnosis]] can lead to the wrong treatment.
She asked for a second opinion on the [[diagnosis]].
Getting a [[diagnosis]] finally explained years of tiredness.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Поставить диагноз» — make a diagnosis или просто diagnose. Put a diagnosis — калька с русского.

collocationTask.prompt: The doctor could not ___ a diagnosis without an X-ray.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Диагноз «ставят» глаголом make: make a diagnosis (или reach, give). Put, do и set — кальки с «поставить» и «сделать».

nuance.text: After the scan, the doctor explained her [[diagnosis]] in simple terms.
nuance.explanationRu: Diagnosis — сам диагноз, вывод врача. Diagnostics — диагностика как набор тестов или область: car diagnostics, diagnostics software.

reverse.text: The garage runs computer [[diagnostics]] on every car it services.
reverse.explanationRu: Компьютерная проверка систем машины — diagnostics. Diagnosis — вывод о том, что именно сломалось или чем человек болен.

fixIt.text: The doctor said the [[diagnose]] was not serious and sent me home.
fixIt.explanationRu: Diagnose — глагол. Существительное «диагноз» — diagnosis: the diagnosis was not serious.

wordFormation.text: A quick [[diagnosis]] can save a patient's life.

rewrite.original: The doctor couldn't say what was wrong with me until the test results came back.
rewrite.frame: The doctor couldn't ____ until the test results came back.
rewrite.explanationRu: Поставить диагноз — make (или give, reach) a diagnosis.

definitionEn: to control or decide how something happens or what is possible
senseNote: Базовое значение — диктовать текст (dictate a letter). Здесь — определять, обусловливать: the budget dictates where we go.
situation: Money, rules, the weather or other circumstances decide what choices people have or what happens.

examples.text: Our budget will [[dictate]] where we go on holiday this year.
In this industry, customer demand [[dictates]] how much we produce each month.
Common sense [[dictates]] that you shouldn't drive in a snowstorm.

texts: The weather will [[dictate]] whether the concert goes ahead.
Don't let fear [[dictate]] your career choices.
Local laws [[dictate]] how tall new buildings can be.

badCollocation.noteRu: Конструкции dictate someone to do something нет. Нужно force или order someone to leave, либо dictate what someone does.

collocationTask.prompt: Circumstances will ___ what we do next.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Circumstances dictate — обстоятельства определяют, что делать. Command — приказывать, prescribe — предписывать (о законе, враче), а tell требует того, кому говорят: tell us.

nuance.text: Tight deadlines often [[dictate]] how carefully we can check our work.
nuance.explanationRu: Dictate (о неодушевлённом) — определять, ставить условия: сроки dictate, насколько тщательно мы проверяем работу. Order — приказывать людям или заказывать.

reverse.text: The officer [[ordered]] the crowd to move back.
reverse.explanationRu: Приказать людям что-то сделать — order someone to do something. Конструкции dictate someone to do нет.

fixIt.text: The size of the venue will [[define]] whether we can invite everyone.
fixIt.explanationRu: Define — давать определение, а не «определять, решать». Когда обстоятельства решают за нас, говорят dictate (или determine).

rewrite.original: The weather will decide whether we eat outside.
rewrite.frame: Whether we eat outside will ____ the weather.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив: will be dictated by — будет определяться чем-то.

definitionEn: a person who tells others what to do and will not accept any disagreement
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — диктатор, правитель с неограниченной властью. Здесь — о властном человеке, который всеми командует.
situation: You complain about a boss, parent or partner who controls everything and never listens to anyone else.

examples.text: Our new manager is a bit of a [[dictator]] — nobody dares to question her decisions.
Their father was a [[dictator]] at home, deciding everything from their hobbies to their friends.
The captain behaved like a [[dictator]], giving orders and punishing anyone who disagreed.

texts: Don't be such a [[dictator]] — let the others choose the film.
The chef ran his kitchen like a [[dictator]].
My sister turns into a little [[dictator]] when she plans a trip.

badCollocation.noteRu: Диктор на радио или ТВ — announcer или newsreader. Dictator — диктатор, тиран.

collocationTask.prompt: She runs the office like a ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Run something like a dictator — управлять деспотично. Dictation — диктант, dictionary — словарь, diction — дикция; о людях так не говорят.

nuance.text: A good manager listens to the team; a [[dictator]] just gives orders.
nuance.explanationRu: Leader — лидер, за которым идут добровольно. Dictator — тот, кто командует и не терпит возражений; слово всегда неодобрительное.

reverse.text: She's a natural [[leader]] — people trust her and follow her willingly.
reverse.explanationRu: Того, за кем охотно идут, называют leader. Dictator подчиняются из страха, а не из доверия.

fixIt.text: Our coach is a real [[dictatorship]] — nobody is allowed to argue with him.
fixIt.explanationRu: Dictatorship — диктатура, система правления. О человеке-деспоте говорят dictator.

wordFormation.text: Staff complained about the director's [[dictatorial]] style of management.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How's the new flatmate? Is he easy to live with?"
options: Regrettably, his dictatorial tendencies render cohabitation somewhat arduous.
Not really. He's a bit of a dictator about the cleaning rota and the heating.
Yes, he's a total dictator, so he lets us decide everything.
reply.explanationRu: A bit of a dictator — властный, всё решает сам. В третьем ответе противоречие: диктатор никому не даёт решать, а первый звучит слишком книжно для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: to recognise or show what makes things unlike each other
senseNote: В бизнесе differentiate ещё значит «выделять (продукт) среди конкурентов»; здесь — различать, видеть разницу.
situation: Someone can tell two similar things apart, for example real and fake news, or two similar sounds.

examples.text: Very young children often cannot [[differentiate]] between fantasy and reality.
It is getting harder to [[differentiate]] real news from clever fakes.
Doctors must [[differentiate]] a harmless mole from a dangerous one.

texts: Some colour-blind people cannot [[differentiate]] red from green.
The course teaches you to [[differentiate]] between facts and opinions.
It is hard to [[differentiate]] the twins until they speak.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Различить» силуэт в темноте или слова в шуме — make out. Differentiate — видеть разницу между вещами.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Differentiate (или distinguish) between right and wrong — отличать добро от зла. Divide, separate и compare с between в этом смысле не употребляют.

nuance.text: At six months, babies can already [[differentiate]] between familiar and unfamiliar faces.
nuance.explanationRu: Differ — самим отличаться: Our opinions differ. Differentiate — видеть или проводить различие между вещами.

reverse.text: Prices [[differ]] a lot from one shop to another.
reverse.explanationRu: Цены сами по себе отличаются — differ. Differentiate требует того, кто видит разницу.

fixIt.text: Can you [[distinct]] a real diamond from a fake one?
fixIt.explanationRu: Distinct — прилагательное «отчётливый, особый». Глагол «отличить одно от другого» — differentiate (или distinguish).

wordFormation.text: There is little [[differentiation]] between the two phone models.

reply.context: In a job interview, the recruiter asks: "How do you check whether a news story is reliable?"
options: Dunno, I just kinda differentiate stuff, you know?
I compare several sources, so I can differentiate facts from opinions.
I differentiate the story to all my colleagues on social media.
reply.explanationRu: Differentiate facts from opinions — отличать факты от мнений. Differentiate не значит «рассылать», а первый ответ слишком небрежен для собеседования.

rewrite.original: Many people can't tell the difference between the two languages.
rewrite.frame: Many people can't ____ the two languages.
rewrite.explanationRu: Differentiate between A and B — видеть разницу между ними.
